{{nihongo|'''Narumi Shrine'''|成海神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Owari Province]].

'''Narumi Shrine''' (なるみじんじゃ) is a Shinto shrine in Narumi-cho, Midori Ward, {{ill|Nagoya|Q11751|qid=Q11751}}, Aichi Prefecture. It is identified with the "Narumi Shrine" listed in the {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}} for Aichi District, Owari Province.

=== History ===
A late source says Narumi Shrine was one of ten shrines established in connection with the return of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kusanagi sword}} to {{ill|Atsuta Shrine|abstract|Q482065|ar|أتسوتا جينغو|az|Atsuta məbədi|cs|Svatyně Acuta|de|Atsuta-jingū|eu|Atsuta santutegia|fa|معبد آتسوتا|fr|Atsuta-jingū|hu|Acutai nagyszentély|id|Kuil Atsuta|it|Santuario di Atsuta|ja|熱田神宮|ko|아쓰타 신궁|la|Atsuta Templum|or|ଆତ୍ସୁତା ଶାଳ|pl|Atsuta-jingū|pt|Santuário de Atsuta|simple|Atsuta Shrine|th|ศาลเจ้าอัตสึตะ|tr|Atsuta Tapınağı|uk|Святилище Ацута|zh|熱田神宮|qid=Q482065}} in 686. It was first at Tenjinyama near the Ougigawa River, where remains of Narumi temple ruins have been linked to a former shrine-temple complex.

The ''Engishiki Jinmyocho'' lists "Narumi Shrine" in Aichi District, and this is widely taken to refer to this shrine. In medieval times, Narumi Castle was built and the shrine is said to have been moved to present Otoyama. Narumi Hachimangu was treated as a separate shrine related to Narumi Shrine.

From medieval to early modern periods it was also called "Togu Daimyojin" and served as the ujigami of Narumi village. It received the rank of Shoichii from the Yoshida house in 1716.

A local tradition records that Yamato Takeru composed poems at Narumi Inlet and crossed by boat toward Odaka. The annual autumn festival includes an "Ofune-nagashi" rite in which a small wooden boat is floated down the river in memory of this legend.

=== Annual events ===
* Setsubun festival (around February)
* Summer chinowa rite (mid-July)
* Narumi festival (second Sunday of October)
* Grand festival and Ofune-nagashi ritual (around October 10)

=== Subsidiary shrines ===
Includes numerous precinct and outside shrines such as Shinmei, Kumano-Hyuga, Hakusan, Hachiman, Sumiyoshi, Atago, Kitano, Koyasu, Tenjin (outside precinct), Togu Inari, and others.

=== Cultural properties ===
* Narumi Festival float events (Urahata side) and floats of Tange, Kitaura, Hanai, and Jonoshita - Nagoya City designated intangible folk cultural property
* 1557 document by {{ill|Imagawa Yoshimoto|Q1054305|qid=Q1054305}} confirming shrine lands
